title: Maryland, other states again sue administration over electric vehicle infrastructure funds
summary: Maryland joined 15 states and Washington, D.C., to sue the Trump administration for withholding billions in federal funds that are supposed to help states build out their electric vehicle infrastructure.
content:
by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters December 17, 2025

by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters December 17, 2025

Maryland joined 15 states and Washington, D.C., to sue the Trump administration for withholding billions in federal funds that are supposed to help states build out their electric vehicle infrastructure.

The suit, filed Tuesday in the U.S. District Court of Washington in Seattle, says the U.S. Department of Transportation and the Federal Highway Administration are sitting on funds that were approved by Congress in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law under former President Joe Biden (D).

It’s the second suit by essentially the same group of states, who sued in May over the administration’s refusal to release $5 billion in funding appropriated under the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program. The court in June issued issued a preliminary injunction against the government’s attempts to hold that money.

The new suit targets two programs that the state say the federal departments have indefinitely put on hold wihtout providing a justification — the $1.8 billion Charging and Fueling Infrastructure (CFI) Discretionary Grant Program and the Electric Vehicle Charger Reliability and Accessibility Accelerator Program, which was supposed to be funded with 10% of the $5 billion in the NEVI program.

“The Trump administration has unlawfully frozen millions of dollars to build charging stations in communities and along travel corridors throughout Maryland. These projects provide an important source of employment and improve our air quality,” Attorney General Anthony Brown (D) said in a statement Wednesday. “We’re suing to unlock this funding and protect Maryland’s clean energy future.”

A representative with the Department of Transportation did not immediately respond for comment Wednesday.

The funding delays stem from an executive order President Donald Trump signed on Jan. 20, his first day back in office. The order, called “Unleashing American Energy,” sought to “eliminate the electric vehicle mandate.” It directed all agencies to “review their processes, policies, and programs for issuing grants, loans, contracts, or any other financial disbursements of such appropriated funds for consistency with the law,” according to the suit. “In short, the President directed agencies to withhold congressionally appropriated NEVI and CFI funds as a tool to terminate programs the President dislikes.”

Tuesday’s suit says Maryland was awarded $56 million to support the deployment of community and corridor charging for vehicles. Brown said those funds were to be used to install 91 new electric vehicle charging stations, repair 44 broken charging ports and build truck charging depots along the Interstate 81 and Interstate 78 freight corridors.

States signed on to the lawsuit filed in May and on Tuesday include Maryland, Washington, D.C., Arizona, California, Colorado, Delaware, Illinois, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin. The May suit also included Hawaii, Minnesota and New Mexico; the latest suit included Massachusetts, Michigan and Pennsylvania.
